title: Debug: The Sales Department Query Returns Nothing
description:
Someone wants every employee in the Sales department, but this query returns zero rows even though Sales clearly has employees. Find the bug and fix it.

Name the column `name`. Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT e.name
FROM employees e
JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.dept_id
WHERE LOWER(d.name) = 'sales';
hint: The `=` operator compares TEXT byte-for-byte by default in SQLite — 'sales' and 'Sales' are not equal. Normalize both sides (or at least the column) with LOWER() before comparing to a lowercase literal.
schemaSql:
CREATE TABLE departments (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  location TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE employees (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  title TEXT,
  salary INTEGER,
  dept_id INTEGER,
  manager_id INTEGER,
  hire_date TEXT
);

tests.name: Department with no employees
Employees with NULL department and NULL salary
Single employee, single department
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Solo','Engineer',100000,1,NULL,'2022-04-01');

tests.name: Duplicate names and same hire dates
Zero and negative salaries, boundary dates
Department name in all uppercase — 'SALES' does not match 'sales'
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'SALES','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Eve','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Finn','E',90000,2,1,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Mixed case — 'Sales' is the original bug
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'Sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Eve','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: No 'Sales' department at all — empty result is correct
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'HR','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Eve','E',100000,1,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Department name with lowercase 'sales' — both queries work
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'Engineering','Austin'),(2,'sales','Denver');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Eve','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01');

tests.name: Multiple department name casings
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO departments VALUES (1,'engineering','Austin'),(2,'SALES','Denver'),(3,'Hr','Austin');
INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Eve','E',100000,2,NULL,'2020-01-01'),(2,'Finn','E',90000,2,1,'2020-01-01');
